Utilization of the Long Spur Ridge site would create construction and operational impacts similar to those at the proposed Bad Creek site. Turbidity created from construction would adversely affect the water quality and biota in about 3.4 miles of the Thompson River and its tributaries within the proposed reservoir area and about 1.8 miles of stream between the dam site and Lake Jocassee.

During operation, continual releases from the upper reservoir would be required in order to maintain flow in the Thompson River below the dam. Without such releases, the flow would be limited to seepage from the upper reservoir and local inflows in the stream reach involved. Releases of water to the Thompson River from the upper reservoir could also cause some changes in downstream water quality depending upon the quality of the upper reservoir water.
8.3.1.4 Scenic and Esthetic Resources
Flow and channel characteristics indicate the Thompson River to be of the larger headwater pool and riffle type, surrounded by moderate to steep slopes that support moderate to dense vegetation, forming a symmetrical tight enclosure
